children: 2204 GMT - The Reserve Bank of Australia has acknowledged that government spending is contributing to an excess of demand in the economy. The bank's chief economist, Sarah Hunter, said in a television interview that "government spending is part of demand, and it's that imbalance between demand and supply that we're really trying to tackle right now." The comments come ahead of a policy meeting in early November where traders see a strong chance the RBA will deliver a fifth interest rate rise for the year. Last week, the RBA said the inflation outlook had become "materially worse." (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
RBA Says Government Spending Contributing to Excess Demand — Market Talk

2204 GMT - The Reserve Bank of Australia has acknowledged that government spending is contributing to an excess of demand in the economy. The bank's chief economist, Sarah Hunter, said in a television interview that "government spending is part of demand, and it's that imbalance between demand and supply that we're really trying to tackle right now." The comments come ahead of a policy meeting in early November where traders see a strong chance the RBA will deliver a fifth interest rate rise for the year. Last week, the RBA said the inflation outlook had become "materially worse." (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
